data.description: A blowout US jobs report fueled expectations for another Fed rate hike as Wall Street reeled from a nearly $4 trillion technology selloff and questions mounted about the AI trade, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Algorand Foundation Closes Forum and Advisory Council, Pauses XGov Grants
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing The Defiant, the Algorand Foundation announced it will close its community forum and advisory council. It will pause XGov grants on December 6, shelve Project King Safety, and maintain staking reward support through January 2028.

data.title: Citi Cuts Three-Month Copper Forecast to $13,300 per Tonne, Sees Surpluses in 2027 and 2028
data.description: According to Jin10, Citi lowered its copper price forecast for the next three months to $13,300 per tonne from $14,500 and expects copper market surpluses in 2027 and 2028. Citi had previously held a neutral view on copper, forecast a short-term price of $14,000-$15,000 per tonne, and expected stronger copper supply growth in 2027.

data.title: San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly: September Rate Hike Was Right, Previous Meeting’s Hold Was Appropriate
data.description: According to Jin10, San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly said a rate hike in September was the right move and keeping rates unchanged at the previous meeting was also appropriate.

data.title: San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly: Tariffs, War and AI Add Uncertainty, but Inflation Is More Persistent Than Expected
data.description: According to Jin10, San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly said tariffs, war, and artificial intelligence are creating uncertainty, but inflation is more persistent than expected.

data.title: Mary C. Daly: Fed Ready to Raise Rates Further If Needed, Decisions Require Caution
data.description: According to Jin10, San Francisco Fed President Mary C. Daly said the Fed is prepared to raise rates further if necessary and that monetary policy still needs tightening, but more information is needed to determine how much further tightening is required and when to act. Daly stressed that the Fed must proceed cautiously.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Bessent and Greer Raise China Deal Concerns With He Lifeng
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer spoke with China’s Vice Premier He Lifeng, raising concerns about Beijing’s recent actions and the importance of implementing commitments under a deal reached a year ago in Busan, South Korea, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Treasuries Decline as Strong Jobs Data Bolsters Tech Rebound
data.description: Treasuries gave back part of this week’s steep gains, driven by haven demand, as strong jobs data supported a rebound in technology shares, Bloomberg reported. JPMorgan Asset Management portfolio manager Priya Misra discussed Treasuries as a safe-haven trade amid AI volatility.

data.title: STOCKS | European Shares Fall Friday, Trimming Weekly Gains as Volatility Stays Below U.S. Markets
data.description:
European shares fell Friday, erasing most of their weekly gains as global stocks declined and volatility rose amid concerns that a Democratic sweep of Congress in the United States could affect AI trades. According to Sina Finance, the Stoxx Europe 600 fell 1% at the close, less than the S&P 500’s 4.4% drop on Thursday and the Nasdaq 100’s 6.4% plunge, its worst single-day performance since March 2020. By the European close, the two U.S. indexes had risen about 0.9% and 1.9%, respectively.

Most European sectors fell Friday, while travel and leisure stocks gained. The Stoxx 600 pared losses as U.S. stock futures rose, even as resilient U.S. economic data reinforced bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

Global markets saw sharp swings this week as investors rapidly exited AI trades and moved into more defensive assets. MPPM Head of Trading Guillermo Hernandez Sampere said portfolio reallocation was to be expected and high volatility could persist for several more days, but the risk of a prolonged correction did not yet appear high.

Teleperformance SE fell 15% after lowering its full-year sales growth guidance. Glanbia Plc fell 8.5% after Morgan Stanley downgraded the Irish nutrition products maker to underweight.

Panmure Liberum strategist Joachim Klement said investors were tired and few new buyers were entering AI trades, adding that this was bearish for technology stocks and the broader market.

Despite Friday’s decline, European equities are becoming one of the more attractive markets. With technology stocks highly volatile, stable industrial companies, banks, defensive leaders and the region’s many commodity companies are considered attractive.

data.title: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar Says Midterm Results Will Not Change Data Center Investment Plans
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing CNBC, OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar said on Friday that the company’s AI infrastructure investment plans would not change based on the U.S. midterm election results. OpenAI will continue working with major hyperscale cloud providers and use financing to meet customer demand for AI. Friar said the election outcome would not significantly affect the business, while the company would step up engagement with local communities and work to build trust as data centers receive more attention.

In the midterms, only one of 41 local data center-related ballot measures across 10 states did not support restricting construction or opposing measures in favor of development. Voters’ main concerns included higher electricity bills, environmental damage and effects on employment.

Friar said OpenAI confidentially filed an IPO application with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission in June and is considering a 2027 listing. The company is also discussing a new funding round at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation. She said demand for AI is real and continues to grow.

data.title: Nvidia, Moderna, IonQ, Airbnb and Firefly Aerospace Lead Midday Stock Moves
data.description: According to CNBC, Nvidia rebounded more than 3% Friday, returning to positive territory for 2026. Moderna gained 7% after beating third-quarter earnings estimates and raising its 2026 revenue growth outlook to 15% to 25%, from no more than 10%. IonQ rose 17% after lifting its full-year revenue guidance to $505 million to $515 million, above analysts’ $456.2 million estimate. Airbnb jumped 11% as third-quarter earnings of $3.16 per share and revenue of $4.87 billion topped estimates. Firefly Aerospace surged nearly 30% after announcing a roughly $1.3 billion agreement with AST SpaceMobile to provide 36 rocket engines and license the engines’ intellectual property.

data.title: Canada Plans One-Time Permanent Residency for Up to 200,000 Temporary Residents
data.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government plans to grant permanent residency to as many as 200,000 temporary residents by the end of 2027, in addition to its annual immigration target, Bloomberg reported.
